title: Hoysala Kingdom
capsule: The Hoysala kingdom was a medieval Hindu dynasty that dominated the Deccan plateau of present-day Karnataka from the early twelfth century, reaching its height under Vishnuvardhana (r. c. 1108–1152) and his successors Veera Ballala II (r. 1173–1220) and Veera Ballala III (r. 1292–1343). The Hoysalas are renowned for their distinctive star-shaped temple architecture, exemplified at Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura, which UNESCO inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2023. The dynasty was fatally weakened by the repeated raids of Malik Kafur (1310–1311) and finally extinguished when the last ruler Veera Ballala III was killed in battle with the Madurai Sultanate in 1343, with their territories absorbed into the nascent Vijayanagara Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Hoysala realm is attested through abundant copper-plate grants and stone inscriptions, giving good coverage of the Karnataka heartland, though peripheral zones in Tamil Nadu and Andhra remain less precisely mapped.
